notes: A Time chip now sits at the end of the Convert row. Pick a place from the searchable list — about fifty of them, from London and Lagos to Tokyo and Auckland — and the card shows the time there, the day there, and the gap from your own clock in words: 3 hours ahead of you, the same time as you, 5 hours 45 minutes behind you.
Your own time sits under it, so both clocks are on one screen, and the place you last picked is remembered — reopening the chip shows the same clock instead of an empty card.

The times come from the phone’s own time-zone database, so daylight saving is whatever each place is actually doing that day: London and New York change on their own dates, and neither of them is your date.
Nothing else changed — elevation, location, the level, the unit converter and its six categories, currency, GPS measuring, the AR range finder, permissions and updates are exactly as they were.
